'''''Curio radicans''''',<ref>{{cite web |title=Taxonomy Browser (Curio radicans) |url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?mode=Info&id=405126&lvl=3&lin=f&keep=1&srchmode=1&unlock |website=NCBI Taxonomy Browser |publisher=National Center for Biotechnology Information |accessdate=28 May 2020}}</ref> syn. ''Senecio radicans'', is a succulent plant native to [[Southern Africa]]. A member of the family [[Asteraceae]], the asters, this species is closely related to the common [[Senecio rowleyanus|string of pearls]] and ''[[Curio hallianus]]''. It has multiple tendrils of glossy, banana-shaped leaves. It is commonly known as '''string of bananas''' or '''fishhook senecio'''.

==Description==
[[Image:Curio radicans 1DS-II 5329.jpg|right|thumb|''Curio radicans'' discoid flower]]

''Curio radicans'' has a prostrate growth habit with mat-forming stems 15–30 cm long.<ref name="Sajeva and Costanzo">Sajeva and Costanzo. "Succulents, The Illustrated Dictionary", Sajeva, M. and Costanzo, M., 2000, Timber Press, Inc.</ref> The succulent leaves are arranged alternately on the stem. They are 2-3cm long, with 2 translucent lines on either side, and their shape is a tapering curved cylinder which resembles a [[banana]].

Like other species in the genus ''Curio'', the inflorescences are [[pseudanthia]], clusters of many small flowers on a common receptacle.<ref name="Mace" /> The pseudanthia are small, cinnamon-scented, and white or off-white. They are usually produced in the late winter or early spring, but may sometimes be produced multiple times through the year.<ref name="Baldwin" />

==Habitat and Distribution==
[[Image:Senecio radicans in CapeTown rockery 1.jpg|right|thumb|''Curio radicans'' in Cape Town]]

''Curio radicans'' is native to [[South Africa]], [[Namibia]], and [[Lesotho]].<ref name = powo/><ref name="University of Connecticut">[http://titanarum.uconn.edu/198500742.html University of Connecticut Ecology and Evolutionary Biology Plant Growth Facilities]</ref>
In the arid desert areas of South Africa, including the Karroid central region, the dominant vegetation consists of xerophytic dwarf shrubs and succulents, including many members of the tribe [[Senecioneae]]. In these areas of very low moisture, the grasslands typical of other areas of Africa give way to areas in which grass is subdominant to these drought-tolerant plants, which are frequently spaced far apart with wide expanses of sandy or rocky stretches in between.<ref name=Bews>Bews. "Plant Forms & Their Evolution In South Africa", Bews, John William, 1925, Longmans, Green and Co.</ref>

''C. radicans'' is frost-tender and cannot withstand freezing temperatures (below {{convert|0|C|F}}), restricting it to areas where the annual temperatures do not drop below this point.<ref name="Baldwin" />

==Cultivation==
Like most members of the ''Curio'' genus, ''C. radicans'' is relatively hardy and easy to grow, making it a popular [[ornamental plant]].<ref name="Mace">Mace. "Cactus and Succulents: A Care Manual", Mace, Tony and Suzanne, 2001, Laurel Glen Publishing</ref>  It may be grown as a groundcover in warm climates, or as a [[houseplant]] in pots and hanging baskets.<ref name="Baldwin">Baldwin. "Succulent Container Gardens", Baldwin, Debra Lee, 2010, Timber Press, Inc.</ref>

This species is grown more for the color, shape, or texture of its foliage than for its blooms, which are small, white, and not very showy.<ref name="Baldwin" /><ref name="Sajeva and Costanzo" />
